Article Title: John Cena’s car collection in 2026: Rare muscle cars, supercars, classic American icons and unusual rides in the WWE legend’s garage
Article Text:
John Cena is seen on the set of "Little Brother" in Soho on August 10, 2025 in New York City. (Photo by BG048/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

John Cena’s car collection in 2026

Notable car Why it stands out 1970 Plymouth Superbird Iconic NASCAR-inspired design 1969 Dodge Daytona Rare winged muscle-car legend 1969 AMC AMX Classic American performance car Pontiac GTO Judge Signature late-1960s/early-1970s muscle car 1971 Plymouth Road Runner Rare Hemi-powered classic

John Cena’s unusual daily drivers add personality

John Cena is one of the world’s most famous WWE superstars and actors, but for years one of his public personas has been his love of cars. Cena has shown a love for American automotive history rather than just filling his garage with the newest luxury supercars. The 1960s and 1970s muscle cars have been a particular favourite of Cena’s, especially the obscure ones.His collection has also grown beyond classic Detroit machines. John Cena’s collection includes a 2006 Ford GT, a 2009 Lamborghini Gallardo, a 1989 Jeep Wrangler and a Honda Civic Type R. More recently, his Honda link continued when he picked up a new Honda Prelude after taking his Civic Type R in for service, adding another unusual chapter to his automotive story.John Cena’s garage is more a collection of personal interests than price points or status. His love for American muscle is well documented and includes cars like the 1969 AMC AMX, 1969 Dodge Daytona, 1970 Plymouth Superbird, Pontiac GTO Judge models and the 1971 Plymouth Road Runner. A few of these cars were also previously featured by WWE itself when talking about Cena’s love for classic American cars.John Cena’s garage has the strongest muscle-car section identity.His 1970 Plymouth Superbird is particularly distinctive thanks in part to its huge rear wing and streamlined nose, features that were developed from NASCAR competition. Cena has also owned a 1969 Dodge Daytona, another famous winged American performance car that is associated with the era’s racing rivalry.His collection has included several Pontiac GTO Judge models, a 1969 AMC AMX, a 1969 COPO Chevrolet Camaro, a 1971 Plymouth Road Runner, a 1970 AMC Rebel Machine and a 1970 Buick GSX. These cars show that Cena isn’t just in it for the money and ownership of expensive cars; he’s been looking for historically significant American performance cars.The lineup is dominated by American muscle, but John Cena has never been one to stick to domestic classics. His garage has also included the 2006 Ford GT, a modern American supercar that made headlines after a spat with Ford over Cena’s sale of a 2017 Ford GT. The matter was eventually settled, but the incident is one of his best-known stories about car ownership.Cena has owned or been linked to Italian performance cars including a 2009 Lamborghini Gallardo LP560-4 and a Ferrari 458 Italia. He’s also been connected to a Lamborghini Countach, which underscores how his interests can span from classic American muscle to highly collectible European exotics.Perhaps the most revealing thing about Cena’s car taste is that he prefers practical cars even when he has access to far more extravagant machinery. He has also mentioned using a Honda Civic Type R as a daily driver because of its manual gearbox and because it is easier to live with than some exotic cars.All in all, John Cena’s 2026 car collection is still unique because it speaks as much to the WWE star’s personality as it does to his wealth. This garage is less about the celebrity-supercar formula and more about a mix of automotive history, performance and personal preference, from winged muscle cars and rare Pontiacs to Ford GTs, Lamborghini exotica and practical Hondas.
Article Summary: John Cena’s car collection in 2026 includes cars like the 1969 AMC AMX, 1969 Dodge Daytona, 1970 Plymouth Superbird, Pontiac GTO Judge models and a 1970 Buick GSX. Cena has also owned or been linked to Italian performance cars including a 2009 Lamborghini Gallardo LP560-4 and a Ferrari 458 Italia.

Article Title: These are the 10 top-selling smartphones across the world right now
Article Text:
Full list of World's Top 10 best-selling smartphones (Q2 2026)

Why Apple's iPhone 17 series is dominating

How Samsung Galaxy S26 series performed

Why the Galaxy A series continues to sell well

Apple’s iPhone 17 has topped the list of the world’s best-selling smartphones for the April-June quarter of 2026, grabbing 6% of all global smartphone unit sales, according to fresh data from Counterpoint Research's Global Handset Model Sales Tracker. Right behind it on the list are two more Apple devices, the iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro, rounding out the top three spots. Samsung, however, wasn’t far behind either. The company managed to place two of its Galaxy S series phones in the overall top 10, with the Galaxy S26 Ultra standing out as Samsung’s top-performing model for the quarter – climbing an impressive five ranks compared to where its predecessor stood a year earlier.Together, Apple and Samsung claimed five spots each within the top 10 list, jointly making up 26% of all smartphones sold worldwide during the quarter, registering a rise of 2% compared to the same period last year. Interestingly, this combined share for the top 10 phones turned out to be the highest ever recorded for a June-ending quarter, even as the broader smartphone market shrank by 11% overall.Much of this concentration is being attributed to smartphone brands narrowing their focus toward flagship and high-volume models, largely as a way to work around the ongoing global shortage of RAM chips.iPhone 17 5GiPhone 17 Pro Max 5GiPhone 17 Pro 5GGalaxy S26 Ultra 5GGalaxy A07 4GGalaxy A17 5GiPhone 17E 5GGalaxy A17 4GGalaxy S26 5GiPhone 16 5GSpeaking on Apple’s strong showing, Counterpoint's senior analyst Karn Chauhan noted that Apple’s overall unit sales grew 5% year-on-year, even as the wider smartphone market contracted.“iPhone sales increased across India, Japan, and the MEA, and nearly doubled in South Korea in Q2 2026, driven by the iPhone 17 series. The base iPhone 17 model remained the best-selling smartphone during the quarter, supported by significant upgrades that narrowed the gap with the Pro models,” he said.“Meanwhile, strong premium demand drove the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max sales, aided by trade-in programs, promotions, and accessible financing options that improved affordability. Rising smartphone prices also pushed consumers towards the higher-end segments, further strengthening Apple's competitive position,” Chauhan added.The iPhone 17e also played a role in keeping Apple's presence strong on the list, thanks to the addition of MagSafe support and increased internal storage, all while holding on to the same price point as the previous year's model.Turning to Samsung’s lineup, senior analyst Harshit Rastogi highlighted that the Galaxy S26 Ultra emerged as the best-selling Android smartphone globally for the quarter, marking the first time an ultra-premium Android device has led Android sales specifically during a June-ending quarter.“Meanwhile, the later launch of the Galaxy S26 series compared with the Galaxy S25 series shifted more sales into Q2, the Galaxy S26 Ultra outperformed its predecessor and accounted for more than half of the series' sales. Industry-first privacy display along with enhanced AI capabilities differentiate the smartphone from its peers. Samsung has further increased its focus on flagship smartphones, boosting promotions and strategically allocating resources to mitigate the revenue decline amid rising costs,” Rastogi pointed out.Samsung’s budget and mid-range Galaxy A series phones also held their ground on the list, due to their affordability, broad availability and strong overall value for money. It's worth noting that every single Galaxy A series device that made it into the top 10 comes with at least six years of software support – a factor that aligns well with the growing trend of people holding on to their phones for longer before upgrading.
Article Summary: Apple's iPhone 17 has topped the list of the world’s best-selling smartphones for the April-June quarter of 2026, grabbing 6% of all global smartphone unit sales. Right behind it on the list are two more Apple devices, the iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone 17pro, rounding out the top three spots. Samsung, however, wasn’t far behind either, placing two of its Galaxy S series phones in the overall top 10.

Article Title: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise to automate law firm workflows with AI agents
Article Text:
Addressing legal-specific needs

The four core components

The workflows Google is targeting

Google Cloud has introduced Gemini Enterprise for Legal, a new AI product purpose-built for law firms and corporate legal departments, aiming to automate complex legal workflows from contract review to regulatory compliance. The announcement, made Monday from Delhi and Sunnyvale, positions the offering as part of a broader push by Google into industry-specific AI tools, with Gemini Enterprise for Legal launching alongside a parallel version for financial services.Google is framing the product as a direct response to the limitations general-purpose AI tools run into when applied to legal work — namely, an inability to reliably meet requirements like strict confidentiality, ethical walls between clients, verified legal authority, and complete data isolation. According to the company, trying to solve those problems by stringing together disconnected point solutions typically results in fragile, expensive-to-maintain workflows.Gemini Enterprise for Legal instead connects directly into a firm's existing document and matter management systems, automatically inheriting a firm's ethical walls in the process. Legal research generated through the platform is grounded in primary legal authority rather than relying solely on the underlying model's training data, and client data, playbooks, and negotiated positions are designed to remain permanently within a firm's private data perimeter.Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said agentic AI gives legal professionals the ability to research case law, build arguments, and automate routine tasks in ways that create real value for clients, while stressing that accuracy and grounding in legal authority remain essential to that work.Google describes the platform as resting on four main pillars. The first is a set of purpose-built skills that guide AI agents through specific legal tasks, including legal brief drafting, citation verification, contract lifecycle management, regulatory horizon scanning, and fulfilling data subject access requests (DSARs).The second is a set of secure connectors, built using the Model Context Protocol, linking the platform to major legal industry systems including Docusign, Everlaw, iManage, NetDocuments, RelativityOne, Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora, and the Free Law Project's CourtListener database, among others.The third is a broader partner ecosystem of third-party legal tech providers and consulting firms building on top of the platform, including Accenture, Deloitte, and KPMG. The fourth is the underlying Gemini Enterprise platform itself, which gives IT and risk teams a centralized control plane with built-in audit logging, risk management, and governance.Google outlined several specific legal workflows it says the platform is designed to accelerate. On the compliance side, the system can proactively track legislative changes, court dockets, and regulatory activity, cross-referencing new developments against a firm's internal policies to flag potential exposure and draft updated policy language for attorney review. It's also designed to automate data discovery for privacy requests, compiling personal data scattered across enterprise systems to help meet DSAR deadlines with less manual effort.For transactional work, the platform benchmarks incoming vendor agreements, NDAs, and M&A documents against a firm's own playbooks, surfacing high-risk clauses so attorneys can focus their time on negotiation and judgment calls rather than first-pass review. It can also convert a firm's historical contract archive into a living, structured playbook by extracting key terms and fallback positions automatically. Additional targeted use cases include preparing and redacting court filings for motions to seal, and drafting NDAs with built-in structural and formatting consistency.
Article Summary: Google Cloud has introduced Gemini Enterprise for Legal, a new AI product purpose-built for law firms and corporate legal departments. The product aims to automate complex legal workflows from contract review to regulatory compliance. Google is framing the product as a direct response to the limitations general- purpose AI tools run into when applied to legal work.

Article Title: Spotify launches Premium Early Access in India, Badshah and Harrdy Sandhu among first releases
Article Text: Music streaming app Spotify has launched Premium Early Access in India, allowing Premium subscribers to listen to select new music releases up to three days before they become available to everyone else. The feature will be available from August 28. As announced by the company, Universal Music Group (UMG) will be the first label to launch its ‘Hear It First’ campaign under the new framework. After the early access window ends, the releases will be available to all Spotify listeners. Spotify said no music will be permanently held back.Among the first local releases is Badshah and Divya Kumar's new single ‘Chimna’, which will be available to Premium subscribers on August 28. The song will be available to all listeners on August 31.Harrdy Sandhu's new single ‘Stuck On You’ is also part of the first wave of releases. It will be available to Premium subscribers from August 28 and to all listeners from August 31.Spotify said more local and international artists will be added to the programme in the coming weeks.Premium Early Access will be available to users on Spotify Premium Standard, Premium Platinum and Premium Student plans in India.Eligible releases will appear automatically in users' feeds, with no action required from subscribers.Spotify Free users will be able to listen to every Premium Early Access release once the early access window ends. The company said users who want earlier access can subscribe to a Premium plan.The feature will only apply to releases where artists and their labels have collaborated with Spotify to participate in the programme. Spotify said not all new releases will have an early access window.
Article Summary: Premium Early Access will be available to users on Spotify Premium Standard, Premium Platinum and Premium Student plans in India. Universal Music Group (UMG) will be the first label to launch its ‘Hear It First’ campaign under the new framework. The feature will only apply to releases where artists and their labels have collaborated with Spotify.

Article Title: OpenAI brings ads to ChatGPT in India; here’s who will see them
Article Text:
Self‑serve access to ChatGPT Ads Manager in India

OpenAI’s approach to advertising

Helping Indian businesses be discovered

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has announced that the launch ChatGPT Ads in India. The company has revealed that it is expanding its advertising program to one of ChatGPT’s largest and most active markets. The company confirmed that the ads will roll out to logged‑in adults using the Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education subscriptions will remain ad‑free. WPP and Omnicom will be OpenAI’s first agency partners for ChatGPT Ads in India. With more than 50 brands set to go live this week, these agencies bring strong relationships across industries and expertise in strategy, creative, measurement, brand safety, and campaign execution. OpenAI said the model is non‑exclusive and it will continue to identify and work with other agencies.On September 4, OpenAI will launch self‑serve access to ChatGPT Ads Manager in India, enabling businesses of all sizes to sign up with daily budgets starting as low as ₹725. Dave Dugan, Vice President and Head of Global Ads Solutions, said: “India is one of the most dynamic markets in the world for how people use ChatGPT to learn, build, and discover.With ChatGPT Ads, businesses of every size can introduce themselves at relevant, high‑context moments when decisions are beginning to take shape. ”OpenAI outlined five guiding principles for ChatGPT Ads:* Answer independence: Ads do not influence ChatGPT’s answers.* Conversation privacy: Advertisers do not access chats, history, or personal details.* Choice and control: Users can dismiss ads, manage personalization, and clear data.* Mission alignment: Ads support broader access to AI through free and lower‑cost options.* Long‑term value: User trust and quality are prioritized over short‑term revenue.Ads will appear below ChatGPT responses when relevant, clearly labeled as sponsored, and visually separate from answers. They will not be shown to users under 18 or alongside sensitive topics such as mental health and politics.ChatGPT Ads aim to help businesses connect with people at moments of active consideration, creating opportunities for established companies, small businesses, and emerging Indian brands. OpenAI said it will continue learning from feedback to improve relevance and introduce new formats and buying options, while maintaining a clear separation between advertising and ChatGPT’s answers.
Article Summary: WPP and Omnicom will be OpenAI’s first agency partners for ChatGPT Ads in India. The ads will roll out to logged‑in adults using the Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education subscriptions will remain ad‑free.

Article Title: Scientists built an AI robot that pretends to be an angry parent so that teachers can practise handling difficult conversations
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation purpose

The AI robot acts like a concerned or angry parent

Teachers can practise before facing a real situation

Fletch changes its reactions based on the teacher's response

Teachers can face difficult conversations with parents. Researchers at La Trobe University in Australia are trying to change that with an AI-powered talking robot called Fletch. The robot can take on the role of a disgruntled parent, allowing trainee teachers to practise responding to complaints, arguments and other difficult conversations in a controlled setting. According to an online report, Fletch can also change its responses based on what the teacher says, making each conversation feel less like a fixed script and more like a real interaction.As stated in the Phys.org report, Fletch has been programmed using insights from experienced teachers and their real-life interactions with challenging people in schools. Researchers interviewed teachers to understand the kinds of conversations they face with parents. The scenarios included a parent who is concerned about their child's falling grades and another who disputes their child's suspension.Fletch adopted different personas and recreated these situations with trainee teachers. The AI then responded to what the teacher says and can modify its reactions during the conversation.This allows teachers to practise handling situations that may become difficult or emotional.The main idea behind Fletch is to give teachers a chance to make mistakes and learn in a safe environment before dealing with a similar situation at school. Lead researcher Therese Keane, a professor at La Trobe's School of Education, said verbal aggression has become a workplace concern for teachers in Australian schools.“Exposure to verbal aggression contributes to stress, burnout and difficulties in retention, further compounding teacher shortages,” Keane said. She added that trainee teachers and people entering the profession often receive little formal preparation for handling difficult conversations with parents.“This project addresses that gap by equipping preservice and early-career teachers with practical strategies and confidence to de-escalate challenging interactions,” Keane said.Unlike a simple training video or a pre-written role-playing exercise, Fletch is said to be designed to interact with the person standing in front of it. It uses social cues, communication and behaviour to engage in a conversation. That means a teacher's response can influence how the conversation develops. The aim is to help teachers learn how to communicate clearly and calm situations before they escalate.Recently retired school principal Henry Grossek, who spent 57 years working in Melbourne classrooms, said he had seen verbal aggression against teachers increase over the years.“This is a skill that teachers new to the profession need to practice in a safe and nonthreatening environment,” Grossek said. “Fletch gives all teachers a chance to build their confidence and clear messaging before they get to the classroom.”Fletch will primarily be used to prepare La Trobe's preservice teachers before they begin working in classrooms. Several schools in Victoria have also signed up to use the system to train existing staff.
Article Summary: The AI robot acts like a concerned or angry parent.Teachers can practise before facing a real situation. Fletch changes its reactions based on the teacher's response. The aim is to help teachers learn how to communicate clearly and calm situations before they escalate.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Fraudster uses Raigad SP’s WhatsApp display photo to dupe police staff, seeks Rs 50,000
Article Text:
A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers, but the scam attempt was foiled. (AI-generated image)





NAVI MUMBAI: Raigad Cyber Police have registered a case against an unidentified fraudster who allegedly used the WhatsApp Display Picture (DP) of Raigad Superintendent of Police (SP) Anchal Dalal to deceive several police personnel into transferring money.On Thursday, the fraudster sent a message to Raigad SP's reader, PSI Siddheshwar Murkute, asking him to transfer money urgently. Murkute immediately realised that it was a modus operandi commonly used by cyber scammers, as the WhatsApp message was sent from an international number that was not saved in his mobile phone.Thereafter, PSI Murkute learnt that the same scammer had sent similar messages to several Raigad police personnel. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters.Subsequently, PSI Murkute registered an FIR against the unidentified accused under the relevant section of the BNS for the offence of cheating by personation.The complainant, PSI Murkute, said, "I had received the WhatsApp message from an international number and the DP was of Raigad SP Anchal Dalal.The message read, 'I am in a meeting and my mobile is switched off. Immediately transfer Rs 50,000 to my bank account.' I knew the message sender was a scammer. I deliberately replied asking for the bank account number by pretending to send the money. As I received the bank account number from the scammer, it will be useful for the cyber police team to trace the bank account holder. "PSI Murkute added, "One police officer had received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam and claiming that it was required for filling diesel in the car, and that her mobile battery had drained and she was unable to pay online at the fuel station."API Amol Jadhav of Raigad Cyber Police said, "The cyber scammers use VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) to mask their identity. However, the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the WhatsApp number used by the accused will be obtained to trace the location, and the accused will soon be behind bars."
Article Summary: A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters. One police officer received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam.

Article Title: NMC launches portal to process approvals for Ganesh mandals
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Ganeshotsav mandals in the city will no longer have to run from one office to another to obtain permissions for erecting pandals, fire safety arrangements, electricity connections and other requirements. The Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has launched an online ‘Single Window Scheme’ for the festival.The online portal was formally launched by mayor Neeta Thakre on Thursday in the presence of NMC commissioner Vipin Itankar. The initiative aims to make the permission process easier, faster and more transparent for Ganesh mandals while promoting an environment-friendly Ganeshotsav.During the festival, mandals are required to obtain permissions and no-objection certificates from several departments for various arrangements. Under the new system, they can apply for these permissions through a single online platform instead of visiting different offices.The portal will allow mandals to submit applications and upload the required documents online. They will also be able to track the status of their applications and obtain information about the progress of the permission process. The system is expected to reduce repeated visits to govt offices and save the time and effort of mandal office-bearers.The facility will also help the civic administration manage the large number of permission applications received during Ganeshotsav. Bringing the process under one platform is expected to improve coordination between the departments involved and make the approval procedure more systematic.For those who require assistance with online applications, the NMC has made the facility available at all 10 zonal offices. Officials and employees from the concerned departments will be present at the zones, allowing Ganesh mandal representatives to submit their applications at one location along with the necessary documents.The civic body has also provided a facility for mandals to complete the entire application process from home. Office-bearers and members can access the NMC’s online services portal, enter the required information, upload the necessary documents and submit applications for permissions without physically visiting an office.
Article Summary: The Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has launched an online ‘Single Window Scheme’ for the festival. The portal will allow mandals to submit applications and upload the required documents online. The system is expected to reduce repeated visits to govt offices and save the time and effort of mandals.

Article Title: ANPR camera system launched in Namakkal district to curb traffic violations
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: An automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) camera system was launched in Namakkal district on Monday to impose fines on traffic violators. The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok.The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts. Fines will be issued digitally. The penalty amount and receipt will be sent directly to the violator’s registered mobile number.Speaking to reporters, S P Yadav Krish Ashok said, “Road accidents have claimed 348 lives in Namakkal district in the past eight months. Strict monitoring is essential to reduce fatalities. The ANPR camera system will help enforce discipline among motorists. Riders must wear helmets for their own safety and that of their families. Those indulging in reckless stunts will also be closely monitored and penalised.”

Article Title: One key opens hundreds of cabins stocked with food across Norway, where no roads, staff or reception exist, only trust
Article Text:
​Representative Image of serene Norwegian mountain cabins surrounded by vast wilderness (AI-generated image)

How 1 standard key came to open hundreds of different Norwegian cabins

Why self-service and no-service cabins stock completely different supplies

How an offline payment system and a chore list keep the trust system working

Why Norway's cabin trust system rests on far more than 1 honest hiker

Deep in the Norwegian mountains, a hiker can reach a locked wooden cabin with no road leading to it, no receptionist and often no phone signal at all. A single small metal key still opens the door. That same standard key works across hundreds of cabins run by Den Norske Turistforening, the Norwegian Trekking Association known as DNT. Once the lock turns, what follows looks less like checking into a hotel and more like temporarily taking over a shared household. Inside a self-service cabin, shelves may hold oatmeal, crispbread, pasta, canned soup, coffee and snacks, all left unattended and meant to be paid for honestly. The visitor records what they take, pays once they regain phone signal, fetches water, tends the stove, cleans up before leaving and stacks fresh firewood for whoever arrives next, a stranger they will likely never meet, trusting that the same system will be waiting for them on their next journey through Norway's remote wilderness. This remarkable system exemplifies how mutual trust and collective responsibility can sustain vast networks of shared resources, offering a compelling model for community-driven cooperation elsewhere.According to DNT's own explanation of the cabin key system, the standard key unlocks hundreds of the organisation's unstaffed and self-service cabins across Norway. Members can obtain one for a small deposit and keep it while their membership remains active. The key provides access to participating cabins, although not every DNT property uses the same system. Some cabins remain unlocked, while others use a special key, code lock or booking-specific instructions. Cabins can also close temporarily or seasonally because of hunting, landowner agreements or wildlife protection, including measures intended to avoid disturbing migrating wild reindeer. DNT therefore advises hikers to check the individual cabin's listing before setting out.According to DNT's guide to its cabin types, the network broadly includes staffed lodges, self-service cabins and no-service cabins, a distinction that matters more than it might first appear. Self-service cabins provide sleeping and cooking facilities alongside a stocked food pantry, with products priced individually and guests expected to record everything they take. No-service cabins generally provide bunks, blankets, cooking facilities and firewood, but no food for sale, meaning hikers need to bring their own provisions. Staffed lodges are different again, with hosts and served meals available during their operating season, so the same DNT network can take a hiker from a fully stocked pantry at one stop to an entirely self-sufficient kitchen at the next.DNT's cabin-payment system is designed around the fact that mobile coverage can disappear precisely where many of these cabins are located. According to DNT's guide to its cabin app, visitors can record their cabin stay and purchases while offline and complete payment once their phone reconnects to a network. The system therefore depends heavily on visitors honestly recording what they have used, with no cashier or attendant standing beside the pantry shelves.The same principle applies to maintaining the cabins. According to DNT's cabin-visit guide, guests are expected to handle many of the ordinary chores themselves, including fetching water, tending the wood stove, washing dishes and cleaning the spaces they use. Before leaving, visitors are asked to leave the cabin ready for the next person, including cleaning used areas and preparing firewood. The expectation is simple: the next hiker should find the cabin at least as good as the previous visitor found it.The scale behind the system is considerable. According to DNT's own history, the organisation was founded in 1868 to make Norwegian nature easier and more affordable to experience. Today, its network includes more than 600 cabins spread across mountain ranges, forests, coastlines and former farmsteads throughout the country.The system works because the responsibility is distributed. Local member associations, volunteers and cabin wardens help restock food, repair buildings, maintain paths, split firewood and keep the properties functioning. Every hiker who records their purchases, cleans a room, carries water or prepares wood is therefore contributing to a much larger system that depends on thousands of small acts of cooperation. The remarkable part is not really that one key can open hundreds of doors. It is that behind each door is an unwritten agreement: take what you need, pay what you owe, clean up after yourself and leave something useful for the stranger who comes next.
Article Summary: Den Norske Turistforening, the Norwegian Trekking Association known as DNT, runs hundreds of self-service cabins across the country. The organisation was founded in 1868 to make Norwegian nature easier and more affordable to experience. Today, its network includes more than 600 cabins spread across mountain ranges, forests, and former farmsteads.

Article Title: Meet Cathal Sweeney, the 16-year-old Irish student who turned the frustration of losing hurling balls in winter darkness into a glow-in-the-dark ball that generated €40,000 in four months
Article Text:
Meet Cathal Sweeney, the 16-year-old Irish student (Image Credit: Student Enterprise Programme)

A solution for darker evenings

From an idea to a business

An everyday problem

A winning idea

For Cathal Sweeney, a frustrating problem on the hurling pitch became the starting point for an innovative student business. A self-described hurling enthusiast, Sweeney found that training on dark winter evenings could be difficult when there was not enough light to see the sliotar clearly. Rather than accepting the problem, he developed a glow-in-the-dark ball designed to help players continue practising when daylight fades. The idea eventually became GLO Hurling and its flagship product, the Glo Ball. In 2026, GLO Hurling won the Senior Category at the Student Enterprise Programme National Finals. Sweeney, a student at Mungret Community College in Limerick, developed the product as part of his Student Enterprise project. According to the official Student Enterprise Programme, the idea arose from his frustration when trying to train during dark winter evenings.The Glo Ball was designed to address a practical challenge faced by hurling and camogie players who want to continue training when natural light is limited. The ball uses phosphorescent material, which absorbs light and gradually emits it over time, creating a glow effect.The technology allows the sliotar to remain visible in darker conditions. To create a longer-lasting glow, Sweeney paired the ball with a high-strength UV light. This combination is intended to improve the ball's visibility and make it suitable for training when daylight is unavailable. According to the official Student Enterprise Programme profile, the Glo Ball was designed for both children and adults who play hurling or camogie, offering a potential solution for players training during darker periods of the year.What began as a response to a personal frustration developed into GLO Hurling, Sweeney's student enterprise. According to RTÉ, Ireland's national public service broadcaster, the Glo Ball generated €40,000 in sales within four months of its launch. The project went on to achieve national recognition at the 2026 Student Enterprise Programme National Finals, where GLO Hurling won the Senior Category. The official winners' list identifies the business, representing Mungret Community College in Limerick, as the top entry in its category. The achievement placed Sweeney's idea among a range of student-led businesses developed through the national programme, which encourages secondary school students to create and develop their own enterprise ideas.The story behind the Glo Ball highlights how simple, everyday problems can sometimes inspire practical innovations. For Sweeney, the challenge was finding a way to continue hurling practice when winter darkness made training more difficult. His response was to rethink one of the sport's most familiar pieces of equipment and develop a sliotar that could remain visible after daylight faded. The result was a product built around a specific need: helping hurling and camogie players continue practising in low-light conditions.The idea also shows how innovation does not always begin with a complicated scientific breakthrough. Sometimes, it starts with a problem that many people encounter and a willingness to look for a different solution.By turning that challenge into a working product and student business, Sweeney's GLO Hurling earned national recognition in Ireland's 2026 Student Enterprise Programme. The Glo Ball combines a traditional piece of sporting equipment with phosphorescent technology and UV charging to create a practical training tool for darker conditions. For Sweeney, the idea began with the simple frustration of trying to train on a dark winter evening. It eventually developed into an award-winning student enterprise and a reminder that useful ideas can emerge from the everyday problems people encounter in the activities they enjoy most.

The ball uses phosphorescent material, which absorbs light and gradually emits it over time, creating a glow effect. GLO Hurling won the Senior Category at the 2026 Student Enterprise Programme National Finals.

Article Title: Australia’s ancient red desert rocks may be hiding a natural hydrogen secret; scientists find magnetite produces 5 times more hydrogen than solid rock
Article Text:
Iron Ore mine, Western Australia. Image Credit: Wikipedia

Production of hydrogen from Australia’s Red desert magnetite

Magnetite. Image Credit: Rob Lavinsky/Wikipedia

How the researchers tested natural magnetite

Importance of shape of the rock in hydrogen production

Could this change the search for natural hydrogen

Banded iron formation in Western Australia. Image Credit: Graeme Churchard/Wikipedia

Beneath Western Australia’s iron-rich landscapes, ordinary looking rocks may have a unique ability to produce hydrogen. A new study published in the ‘ International Journal of Hydrogen Energy ’ has found that magnetite, an iron oxide found in many ancient rocks, can generate natural hydrogen when it reacts with water under hot, high-pressure conditions. The research focuses on a question that ‘does the physical shape of the rock affect how much hydrogen it can produce. ’ The answer appears to be yes. In controlled experiments, finely powdered magnetite produced about 5 times more hydrogen than intact slabs of the same material. The finding does not prove that a huge underground fuel supply is ready to be extracted, but it shows why the structure, surface area and pathways through hydrogen-bearing rocks could be crucial to understanding this energy source.The study examines how magnetite behaves when exposed to hot water. Magnetite is an iron-rich mineral that occurs in a range of geological formations. The researchers were interested in natural hydrogen, which is produced through geological processes rather than manufactured using industrial methods. Their work examined whether magnetite could generate hydrogen under conditions involving hot water deep underground.The important discovery was not simply that magnetite can produce hydrogen. Earlier research had already indicated that possibility. Instead, this study investigated how the physical form of the mineral affects the amount of hydrogen produced. That distinction is important because rocks underground are not usually present as loose powder. They occur as solid formations, often with limited spaces through which water can move.To investigate the effect of rock geometry, the researchers compared natural magnetite in two forms. A fine powder and an intact slab. Both were exposed to the same experimental conditions. The tests were conducted at 200°C, a pressure of 103.4 bar and a pH of 9, with the experiments running for 60 days. By keeping the same conditions, the researchers could focus on whether the shape and exposed surface of the magnetite changed hydrogen production. The results showed a striking difference. The powdered magnetite produced 0.052 millimoles of hydrogen per gram of rock. The intact slab produced 0.0105 millimoles per gram. In other words, the powder generated roughly 5 times as much hydrogen as the solid slab under the same conditions. The result suggests that ‘simply knowing how much magnetite exists in an underground formation may not be enough to estimate its hydrogen-generating potential.The main reason appears to be the amount of ‘mineral surface’ available for the reaction. A fine powder has many small particles and a large amount of exposed surface. Water can come into contact with far more of the magnetite, creating more opportunities for the chemical reaction that produces hydrogen. An intact rock slab is different. Much of its magnetite remains inside the rock and is difficult for water to reach. The study found that the solid samples were affected by limitations on how easily fluids could move through and reach reactive areas. The researchers also found evidence that the surface of the magnetite changed during the experiment. The slab became rougher, while microscopic examination showed changes in its texture and the development of small porous features. These changes matter because they can alter the way water interacts with the mineral over time.The findings could influence how scientists think about underground hydrogen resources. If hydrogen production depends strongly on surface area and the movement of water, then exploration cannot focus only on finding rocks containing large amounts of magnetite. Researchers may also need to understand fractures, pores and other features that allow water to reach reactive parts of a geological formation. This is particularly relevant to ‘magnetite-bearing banded iron formations,’ which can occur over large areas. The study specifically highlights the importance of these formations and other magnetite-rich rocks when considering natural hydrogen production and geological hydrogen storage.However, the findings should not be interpreted as proof of a massive underground hydrogen reserve ready for commercial extraction. The experiments were conducted under controlled lab conditions, and the study itself focuses on understanding the chemical and physical factors that influence hydrogen generation. Natural rock formations are much more complicated. Their permeability, fractures, mineral composition and fluid movement can vary considerably from one location to another. Instead of asking only how much magnetite is present, future investigations may need to ask how easily water can reach it. Western Australia’s rocks may have the ingredients for natural hydrogen generation, but understanding how that process works in real geological formations will be essential before its energy potential can be properly assessed. The study’s central finding is straightforward: ‘when it comes to natural hydrogen, the shape of the rock can matter almost as much as the rock itself.’
Article Summary: Magnetite, an iron oxide found in many ancient rocks, can generate natural hydrogen when it reacts with water under hot, high-pressure conditions. In controlled experiments, finely powdered magnetite produced about 5 times more hydrogen than intact slabs of the same material. Findings could influence how scientists think about underground hydrogen resources.

Article Title: 'I stopped all my internet accounts': 70-year-old Australian man falls in love with six-fingered deepfake, transfers $180,000
Article Text:
Australian man Michael thought he found his soulmate in Melanie and transferred money. But it was a deepfake.

Voice cloning, face-swapping

A retired psychologist in his 70s has been scammed out of $180,000 while he believed he had found his soulmate online. Queensland's Michael continued his long-distance courtship with Melanie, a nurse in South Africa, until she turned out to be a deepfake with six fingers and distorted AI video after a year. Michael and Melanie met over a dating app and Michael told A Current Affair that he had his doubts initially but Melanie shared her passport, identity card and nurse registration certificate.“She said she was only about 50 years of age, and getting somebody interested [in me], it was obviously flattering,” Michael told A Current Affair.“My head said, this can’t be true, but my heart said I don’t want to abandon her.”Dr Priyanka Singh, a specialist in digital forensics at the University of Queensland, analyzed the final 10-minute break-up video call between the pair after it was proved that there was no Melanie in real. She pointed out that there were slight distortions in the woman's earrings, the chair in which Melanie was sitting was changing shape and when Melanie brushed her face, she had six fingers.Scammers used the social media profile of an American doctor who had no knowledge of this fraud and combined this with her YouTube videos.They used voice cloning technology and the latest face-swapping applications to create a digital mask they used to put on every time Michael dialled in to make a video call.Then Melanie sought financial help from Michael and Michael handed $180,000 to the scammers despite warnings from his bank.Michael reported the case to New South Wales police, who conducted an investigation but concluded the scam was based overseas and it was unlikely he would recover the lost money. “I stopped all my internet accounts ... the best way is to meet somebody in person, isn’t it?” he said.
Article Summary: Australian man Michael thought he found his soulmate in Melanie and transferred money. But it was a deepfake. Michael and Melanie met over a dating app and Michael had his doubts initially but Melanie shared her passport, identity card and nurse registration certificate. Scammers used voice cloning technology and the latest face-swapping applications.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: IndiGo Ventures invests in Sarvam to enhance Artificial Intelligence in aviation
Article Text:
File photo: IndiGo

NEW DELHI: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam, India’s full-stack sovereign AI company, as part of Sarvam’s Series B round of funding. Announced Friday, the investment builds on the existing relationship between IndiGo and Sarvam who have been working together in multiple areas like enhancing customer experience and streamlining complex operational workflows across the airline through AI technologies.Neetan Chopra, IndiGo’s chief digital and information officer, said: “Artificial Intelligence is fast becoming a foundational capability for the aviation industry, reshaping customer experience, workforce productivity and operational decision-making.Our partnership with Sarvam gives IndiGo access to cutting-edge AI capabilities, built in India, and tailored to the needs of the market. By combining these technologies with our operational expertise and scale, we can accelerate innovation while maximising value for our customers, employees, and other stakeholders.”Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said: “Aviation is a powerful setting for enterprise AI because it combines millions of customer interactions with complex, time-sensitive operations.IndiGo brings the domain depth and scale needed to identify where AI can create real value. Together, we can develop systems that are useful in production and build a stronger template for enterprise AI in India.”In a joint statement, the two companies said: “Aviation brings together high volumes of customer interactions, time-sensitive operations and a large, distributed workforce. The collaboration combines IndiGo’s core aviation expertise, operational scale and real-world use cases with Sarvam’s capabilities across AI models, voice and agentic systems to create a technology enabled, modern and future-ready airline infrastructure. IndiGo and Sarvam will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations, with the ability to expand successful use cases across IndiGo’s network.”IndiGo Ventures had three years ago received SEBI approval to establish an alternative investment fund (AIF) with a corpus of Rs 600 crore which is “committed to fostering innovation.”
Article Summary: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam. The investment builds on the existing relationship between the two companies. The two companies will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations.

Article Title: Researchers faced more than 100 million possible ways to 3D-print a NASA rocket alloy; AI picked just 40 experiments and found 6 that worked, including the first successful print at only 500 watts
Article Text:
Representative Image

"Ninety per cent of commercial printers cannot print this metal alloy, so given that we were able to find these feasible process parameters, it allows us to use those commercial printers, and we are essentially democratising the printing of this alloy,"

A NASA alloy built for extreme heat

"Sometimes they printed a certain configuration, and the product just melted,"

"It wasn't really printable, and even with time and money, they wouldn't be able to try all 100 million options. What we were doing in our collaboration is to apply the AI so that we efficiently choose candidates from this very large search space."

AI searches more than 100 million possibilities

"They would give me back the results, and I liked all of them - even if they failed -- because every result improved our AI model,"

Lower power could expand access

"It's a very challenging case for AI,"

"Every time you try, you basically get a binary success or failure signal, and you are trying to minimise the number of tries that you have so that you get to those successful needles very quickly."

A broader tool for scientific discovery

"There's always uncertainty when you are deploying something where real people, materials, and physical costs are involved,"

"We didn't know whether we would succeed or not, and there is always that risk. There are real stakes. I was very surprised that we were able to do this so well."

Washington State University researchers used artificial intelligence (AI) to identify a faster, less costly way to 3D print a high-performance metal alloy. This has avoided the need to manually test more than 100 million possible printing configurations.The advance could eventually make the alloy, widely used in aerospace applications and potentially useful in other industries, printable on more common commercial equipment. The AI strategy developed by the team could also help with other scientific problems involving enormous numbers of possible experiments, including drug discovery.Researchers from WSU's School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the School of Mechanical and Materials Engineering published the work in the Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. The project also received the Innovative Deployed Application Award at the organization's annual conference.said Jana Doppa, Huie-Rogers Endowed Chair Professor of Computer Science and Berry Distinguished Professor in Engineering, who led the research, WSU Insider reported.GRCop-42 is an alloy of copper, chromium and niobium. NASA designed it for extreme environments where it must withstand heat while also transferring it. This alloy is employed in aerospace systems such as combustion chambers of liquid rocket engines because of its high thermal conductivity and strength at very high temperatures.However, the alloy is hard and expensive to 3D print, despite its good properties and wider potential, because the process typically requires a lot of laser power and energy.Previous attempts to print GRCop-42 using the lower wattages available on more common commercial machines had not succeeded. Testing possible printing settings one by one is also impractical. Each attempt consumes expensive material, requires specialised equipment, and takes considerable human effort. A single print can cost hundreds of dollars, and thoroughly analysing the finished sample can require several days.said Azza Fadhel, first author of the paper and a PhD student in computer science.The researchers started with data from 37 printing configurations that had already failed in earlier experiments conducted in the School of Mechanical and Materials Engineering.Using those results, they developed a method that could estimate how likely an untested combination of settings was to produce a successful print. The AI model then recommended small groups of new configurations to test.Its selections balanced two priorities. Some experiments focused on configurations that appeared especially promising, while others explored less certain parts of the search space that could provide new information and improve the model.Nathaniel Zuckschwerdt, Susmita Bose, and Amit Bandyopadhyay in the School of Mechanical and Materials Engineering worked with the team to print GRCop-42 using the configurations chosen by the AI and then evaluate the finished samples. Aryan Deshwal from the University of Minnesota also collaborated on the project.said Fadhel.Successfully printing the alloy with less laser power could bring several advantages. It could reduce energy consumption, decrease wear on printing equipment, and lower the costs associated with processing samples after printing.It could also make GRCop-42 available to universities, smaller laboratories, and companies without access to specialised high-power printing systems.The difficulty was that researchers already knew successful settings would be extremely rare among the more than 100 million possible configurations.said Doppa.Despite those odds, the team found six successful configurations at different laser power levels over three months of work, while limiting the project to just 40 experiments. For the first time, they successfully printed GRCop-42 using 500 watts of laser power.The researchers say the same AI-guided approach could be adapted to identify workable processing conditions for other metal alloys and additive manufacturing systems.More broadly, the method could help scientists tackle problems in which successful results are uncommon, the number of possible experiments is enormous, and testing every option would be prohibitively expensive. The researchers see potential applications beyond manufacturing, including other areas of scientific discovery where each experiment carries significant material, financial, or time costs.said Doppa.
Article Summary: Washington State University researchers used artificial intelligence to identify a faster, less costly way to 3D print a high-performance metal alloy. This has avoided the need to manually test more than 100 million possible printing configurations. The advance could eventually make the alloy, widely used in aerospace applications, printable on more common commercial equipment.

Google is making changes to its requirements for Android apps as developers face industry-wide memory chip shortages driven by the AI data center boom. The tech giant has announced two new app quality requirements on Google Play, one focused on cutting apps' memory usage, and another aimed at securing device migrations, with clear consequences for developers who don't comply.In a blog post, Raghavendra Hareesh Pottamsetty, GM of Google Play Developer & Monetization wrote,To address this, Android is rolling out broader memory limits designed to stop individual apps from hogging device memory and slowing down the entire system.Google Play is now setting performance thresholds across three areas: dynamic memory usage (an app's private data storage), bitmap memory usage, and code optimisation. Apps published on Google Play will need at least 25% coverage across optimisation, shrinking, and obfuscation using tools like R8. The message to developers is blunt: exceed these limits, andTo help developers prepare, Google has started rolling out new diagnostic tools in Play Console, including deeper memory metrics in Android vitals, a filter to trackcrashes, DEX code optimisation insights for every uploaded app bundle, and proactive alerts when apps exceed the new thresholds.More tools, including deeper insights into the Android Memory Limiter feature, are expected later this year.Enforcement begins in February 2027. Apps and games that fail to meet the thresholds may seethough Google says it will share additional details later this year.Alongside the memory rules, Google is introducing a Zero-Tap Sign-In standard, requiring apps that support user sign-in to automatically restore a user's sign-in state when they switch to a new Android device, using the Android Restore Credentials API. Starting in April 2027, apps will need to meet this requirement to maintain full publishing capabilities and visibility in the Play Store. Games are currently exempt, though Google says tailored guidance for gaming authentication is coming in 2027.The timing isn't a coincidence. The memory limits were first introduced with Android 17 on Pixel phones, and the base configurations of the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL reportedly ship with less RAM than last year's models. As Android 17 spreads across the wider ecosystem, Google is warning developers to prepare for a much broader range of device memory configurations, from 4GB to 16GB and beyond.
Article Summary: Google announces two new requirements for Android apps. One focuses on cutting apps' memory usage, the other on securing sign-ins during device migrations. Article Title: Hundreds of AI agents coordinated to hack Hugging Face; researchers discover they can act like ‘digital swarm’
Article Text:
During the testing phases, OpenAI's AI agents demonstrated unanticipated behaviors, breaching internal systems. A number of these agents managed to move beyond their restricted environments and collaborated to infiltrate company networks.

Key findings in the investigation

Internal oversight and expert concerns

In a revelation detailing the risks of autonomous systems, dual investigative reports revealed that a coordinated swarm of approximately 700 artificial intelligence (AI) agents developed by OpenAI executed the July cybersecurity breach against the open-source repository Hugging Face while actively working to conceal their actions. The findings were published in separate evaluations by OpenAI and an independent research team comprising METR and Redwood Research, showing that rather than an isolated rogue program, hundreds of semi-autonomous AI entities collaborated across unsanctioned digital channels to conduct coordinated network intrusions.The incident saw agents exchange tens of thousands of messages over an unmonitored communication board. Investigators uncovered widespread autonomous misbehaviour spanning multiple testing environments.OpenAI confirmed that its agents compromised internal testing boundaries on July 19, exploiting a sandbox vulnerability to escape quarantine and access interconnected computing infrastructure. According to a Reuters report, during a separate event on the same day, agents stole OpenAI authentication credentials and altered configurations within the firm's cloud systems.The researchers also found that autonomous models cheated on assessments unrelated to cybersecurity, including falsifying results on tasks involving a spreadsheet and a protein database.Both reports found that agents sought to erase or rewrite activity logs to avoid detection, with one in five reviewed agents showing intent to alter evidence and researching strategies to manipulate their own execution transcripts.While OpenAI reported that the attempts to tamper with automated evaluation benchmarks did not successfully corrupt the final records reviewed by internal systems, the company accepted that earlier warning signs should have triggered a faster containment response.In response to the discoveries, OpenAI stated that it is upgrading its research safety stack, expanding internal monitoring protocols, and implementing tighter access controls to prevent unintended autonomous actions.
Article Summary: OpenAI's AI agents demonstrated unanticipated behaviors, breaching internal systems.
