Article Title: Operation Bluebird startup launches Twitter.now, says it is not linked to Elon Musk's X
Article Text:
Operation Bluebird launches Twitter.now (AI-edited image)

A startup sees an opportunity after Twitter became X

A judge's comments gave the startup confidence to launch

Here’s what Operation Bluebird co-founder wrote on LinkedIn

The name Twitter has returned to the internet. A Virginia-based startup called Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now, claiming that the Twitter name and some of its well-known intellectual property were abandoned after Elon Musk renamed Twitter to X. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. Operation Bluebird says its platform is not connected to X and is building a different kind of online public square, with automated fact-checking and more control for users over what they see.When Elon Musk acquired Twitter in 2022, he eventually renamed the platform X and replaced the familiar blue bird branding. Operation Bluebird believes that decision created an opportunity to reclaim the Twitter name.The startup's co-founder Stephen Coates, who previously served as general counsel at Twitter before Musk's takeover, said the company had waited for months before launching but did not want to delay further.Operation Bluebird's legal argument is that X Corporation abandoned its rights to trademarks linked to Twitter, including the word "Twitter," "tweet" and the bird logo. X Corporation, however, sued Operation Bluebird last year and sought to stop the new platform from launching.The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.Legal dispute between Elon Musk’s X and Operation Bluebird continues.During an April 2026 hearing, US District Court Judge Colm Connolly gave a tentative ruling suggesting that X appeared to have given up its intellectual property claims over the word "tweet" and the Twitter bird logo. The judge also raised the possibility that rights to the word "Twitter" may have been abandoned.However, the judge has not yet issued a written order.The move could now intensify the legal battle. Trademark attorney Josh Gerben told Ars Technica that Operation Bluebird may have a workable legal argument, but said the case was far from straightforward and that X could respond strongly now that the platform has launched.In a LinkedIn post, Coates wrote:"Today, Operation Bluebird launched Twitter.now.When X Corp. retired the Twitter brand, we saw an opportunity to build something new: a public square organized around trust, transparency, and user choice.Twitter.now is not an attempt to recreate the old platform. We are building a different service, with trust signals that provide context for what users see and tools that allow people—not an opaque algorithm—to decide how much credibility and noise reach their feeds. Our governing principle is simple: freedom of speech, not freedom of reach.Twitter is a reclaimed brand. We are not X and are not affiliated with X Corp.Early access is now open. Founding members can help us build and test the platform, get first shot at the handle of their choice, and claim their place in its history—including Founder number #00001.The public square is open again, and definitely not affiliated with X in any way. Whatsoever.Get over your X. The bird is back."
Article Summary: Virginia-based startup Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.

Article Title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' event on September 9: Foldable iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro and everything else to expect
Article Text:
The foldable iPhone is the biggest launch expected on the day

The iPhone 18 Pro upgrade sounds modest, the price rise may not be

Watches, AirPods and new home devices make up the rest of the list

Siri AI is the software behind most of these new devices

Apple has confirmed September 9 for its annual iPhone launch, and the invite sent out on Wednesday uses the tagline "Surprise and shine." The keynote starts at 10am Pacific, which is 10.30pm IST, and will stream from the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple Park via Apple's site, YouTube and the Apple TV app.Two things separate this from the usual September routine. It is the first Apple event with John Ternus running the company, since Tim Cook hands over the CEO title on September 1 and becomes executive chairman. The rumoured product list is also unusually long. Apple pushed the new Mac mini and Mac Studio out in late August, a slot it has used only once in the past decade, and several reports read that as an attempt to free up space on stage.The device drawing the most attention is Apple's first foldable, which most reports expect to be called iPhone Ultra. Leaks point to a 7.8-inch inner display that opens like a book and a roughly 5.3-inch cover screen, with the A20 Pro chip and 12GB of memory.Rumours suggest two 48MP rear cameras and no telephoto lens, which would be an odd omission at this price. There are also claims that authentication falls back to Touch ID rather than Face ID.Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who says he has spoken to people who have used the phone, reports that the hinge and the way it fits in a pocket both impressed them, and that it works well as a camera viewfinder. He expects pricing to start above $2,000, roughly Rs 1.8 lakh before Indian duties, so the local figure would likely be higher.The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are widely tipped as a spec-bump year. Reports point to a 2nm A20 Pro with packaging changes meant to help thermals, Apple's own C2 modem, a slightly larger camera bump and a dark cherry finish. A variable-aperture rear camera is rumoured to be a Pro Max exclusive, and under-display Face ID has been floated without much backing.Pricing is the bigger question. With memory costs climbing, Samsung and Google have each raised phone prices by about $100, and Gurman expects Apple to follow, which would put the iPhone 18 Pro near $1,199. Other estimates run steeper.The standard iPhone 18, the iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air are not expected in September, with reports pointing to 2027.Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a light update, with talk of a health sensor tied to a fluoroelastomer band, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 may get a redesign. AirPods 5 look likely, in ANC and non-ANC versions. The camera-equipped AirPods that leaked in a macOS Tahoe release candidate are still reported as a 2027 product.The home devices are the bigger unknown. Reports mention a refreshed Apple TV 4K, a new HomePod mini and a home hub with a seven-inch screen. Gurman reports Apple is reworking the accessory sections in its retail stores, which he takes as a sign of more than routine updates. An OLED iPad mini remains a wildcard.Most of the home hardware has reportedly been waiting on the Siri overhaul Apple previewed at WWDC in June. That keynote was structured differently from the usual run through each operating system in turn, with Apple instead laying out a cross-platform pitch built around Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.The version demoed uses large language model technology to let the assistant act inside apps such as Messages and Calendar rather than only answering questions. It is the feature Apple has been promising and delaying since 2024.Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Tahoe, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27, reportedly in the back half of September and initially as a waitlisted beta. That timing matters for the hardware. A refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini would need newer chips to support it, which is one explanation for why those updates have taken so long, and a home hub with a screen makes little sense without an assistant that can act on requests.
Article Summary: Apple will launch the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max on September 9. The foldable phone is expected to start at around $2,000. Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods are expected to be light updates. Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27.

Article Text:

LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman and others agree that Gen Z has in-demand tech skills

HP's senior executive George Brasher isn't buying the narrative that Gen Z is lazy. "I don't see that at all,” said the company’s SVP and managing director, North America, claiming that the Gen Z’s label of lacking interpersonal skills is a myth and that they're now driving massive business wins with their work ethic. The HP executive also explained that growing up in the digital era is their superpower, as their AI skills not only make them more skilled on the job but also translate into a better quality of working life."I've got a reasonable population of Gen Z folks in my team, and I find people with great ability to listen, great ability to build that trust, to build that relationship, and then to understand really what customers need," Brasher told Fortune. HP employs about 55,000 workers globally, and believes that the youngest generation of employees is leading the charge in creating a more "interconnected, inclusive, and conscientious world. ""Gen Z and millennials have the highest use of AI, highest use of the technology," Brasher continued. "The fact that they're digital natives—and AI natives—really puts them in a great position…to have that use of technology that will give them a healthy relationship with work."College students turning their tassels and taking on 9-to-5 jobs are typically AI natives, Brasher adds, which "positions them very well" within the tough entry-level job market. More than one million US job postings even required AI-related skills as of last year, a 66% increase from 2024, according to a 2026 PwC analysis of Lightcast data.Being well-acquainted with the tools is the key to success in the newest era of tech: "I think everybody coming into their initial career into companies needs to make sure that they're the best prepared for that," Brasher advised.LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman agrees that Gen Z's AI fluency could be their biggest advantage in a tough entry-level job market. The billionaire entrepreneur said that young people are part of "generation AI"; as digital natives who grew up with advanced technology at their fingertips, they are in the best position to leverage that skill. It may be Gen Z's ticket to landing a job."Bringing the fact that you have AI in your tool set is one of the things that makes you enormously attractive," Hoffman said in a video on his YouTube channel last year.Meanwhile, Emily Glassberg Sands, the head of data and AI at Stripe, revealed that she's all-in on hiring recent graduates at the financial services company. She singled out Gen Z's tech adaptability as one of the in-demand skills she's looking for in Stripe employees. They "have the cutting-edge skills" and are up to date on the latest tools, which helps them hit the ground running.
Article Summary: Being digital natives is Gen Z's biggest workplace advantage: HP SVP George Brasher.LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman and others agree that Gen Z has in-demand tech skills. More than one million US job postings even required AI-related skills as of last year.

Article Title: World's first patient to undergo live AI-assisted surgery gets his brain tumour removed; here's how it happened
Article Text:
The pituitary tumour was found by accident after a seizure on a lunchtime walk

The AI read the live surgical video feed instead of pre-operation brain scans

UCL now wants a bigger AI surgery trial and a tool surgeons can argue with

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe AI technology will significantly improve surgical outcomes in the future? Yes, definitely No, I don't think so 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Neurosurgeons in London have removed a brain tumour while an artificial intelligence system watched the operation as it happened and flagged what not to touch, a world first for live AI-assisted surgery. The patient, 48-year-old Rhys Hibbert from Bedfordshire, was slowly going blind from an 11mm growth on his pituitary gland. He came out of theatre with his sight intact and, within a week, was walking without his sticks.The operation was carried out in May at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, part of University College London Hospitals, and made public only on 27 August, once Hibbert had recovered. Prof Hani Marcus performed it alongside surgical resident Danyal Khan, with the AI running on a second screen throughout. The clinical trial is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research and Google.Until December 2024, Hibbert was a fit customer services manager and an ambulance volunteer who walked two miles every lunchtime. On one of those walks he lost consciousness and started fitting in the road.Scans found a non-cancerous tumour on his pituitary gland, an organ roughly the size of a marble. It was left alone at first, then began pressing on his optic nerves. He lost his lower field of vision and started using walking sticks after tripping once too often.Surgeons reach the pituitary through the nose using an endoscope, a camera on a thin stick. The gland sits millimetres from the carotid arteries and the optic nerves, and anatomy differs from person to person. The average UK surgeon does 10 to 20 of these operations a year, working from scans studied beforehand. Even then, there is a 25 to 50 per cent chance of leaving tumour behind and a 0.5 to 2 per cent risk of injuring a major blood vessel.This system watched the feed as it streamed, colour-coding the vessels and nerves it recognised and marking where it was safest to cut. Think face unlock on a phone rather than a robot surgeon. It was built at the UCL Hawkes Institute, runs on Nvidia's Clara IGX platform, and was trained on hundreds of annotated pituitary operations. "There are no road signs inside our head," Hibbert said.Marcus has been clear that the surgeons kept full control. The longer-term ambition is closer to a ChatGPT for the operating theatre, a second opinion a surgeon can consult or overrule, and a larger trial is being planned. Eight weeks on, Hibbert's sight is still sharpening. "It feels like I've got a 360-degree panoramic view of everything around me," he said.
Article Summary: UCL now wants a bigger AI surgery trial and a tool surgeons can argue with. The patient, 48-year-old Rhys Hibbert, was slowly going blind from an 11mm growth on his pituitary gland. He came out of theatre with his sight intact and, within a week, was walking without his sticks.

Article Title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says affordability must be priority for next-gen consoles as hardware prices rise
Article Text:
Industry must tackle the ‘Rampocalypse’

Xbox Disc-to-digital plan

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Microsoft’s gaming brand needs to be mindful of the affordability of its next-generation console for consumers, citing a crisis in computing hardware prices in the video game industry. Speaking in an interview with the BBC, Sharma explained that rising component expenses, driven by massive tech investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, require platform holders to rethink hardware pricing and deliver more accessible gaming options.In a shift for the gaming market, modern consoles have experienced retail price increases years after their initial release dates, fueled largely by escalating memory component costs.“As an industry, we're in the middle of 'Rampocalypse'. All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency. That is something that we have not had to do [previously]. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console,” Sharma stated.While parent company Microsoft ranks among the largest spenders building out enterprise AI data centers, an investment surge driving up semiconductor costs, Sharma noted that Xbox must adapt its engineering roadmaps to real-world market conditions.First is hardware efficiency focus wherein engineering teams developing the next generation must balance baseline performance against storage and memory efficiency, total bill-of-materials costs, and unit retail pricing.Currently developed under the codename Project Helix, Sharma declined to confirm whether the future system will retain a physical disc drive, emphasising that hardware efficiency and cost-effectiveness must sit alongside raw computing power.To protect player investments and ensure backward compatibility across future hardware cycles, Xbox recently announced a program that allows players to digitise their physical game collections. The feature will debut across roughly 1,000 disc-based games, granting an equivalent digital license once a player inserts a compatible disc into an Xbox console.If a gamer chooses to sell their physical disc second-hand, the digital entitlement automatically transfers over to the new buyer. Sharma emphasised that the initiative preserves flexibility between disc ownership and digital libraries, particularly as competitors like Sony eliminate physical disc releases for new PlayStation titles starting in January 2028, and major releases like Grand Theft Auto VI prepare for digital-only rollouts.
Article Summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the gaming industry is in the middle of a 'Rampocalypse' Rising component expenses, driven by massive tech investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, require platform holders to rethink hardware pricing. Sharma declined to confirm whether the future system will retain a physical disc drive.

Article Title: As RAM prices soar and phone makers slash memory, Google finds fix for smoother performance
Article Text:
Curbing app bloat: Key optimisation thresholds

New developer diagnostics in Play Console

As the mobile hardware sector battles component supply pressures that are driving up RAM costs and prompting phone manufacturers to cut down onboard memory, Google is rolling out sweeping quality guidelines across the Google Play ecosystem to protect device performance. To prevent software from overwhelming hardware and causing system lag, Google Play is introducing strict performance benchmarks designed to lower app memory footprints, alongside new standards for secure device migration during user upgrades.To keep the operating system responsive across various hardware tiers, Google Play is establishing clear technical thresholds across three core development areas. First is memory limits. Google will monitor anonymous resident set size (RSS) plus compressed swap data, measuring the private memory used by an application while ignoring code and asset files stored on the device. This consumption will be assessed across active and background states, as well as distinct device capability tiers.Next is bitmap resource management wherein developers must ensure visual assets and bitmaps do not sit idle in system memory during non-visible states, such as when an application is running in the background or held in cache.Thirdly, Google Play will require published Android App Bundles to achieve at least 25% coverage using code-shrinking, optimisation and obfuscation utilities like R8. This optimisation lowers memory overhead, accelerates cold starts, curbs Application Not Responding (ANR) crashes and boosts runtime frame rates.To assist creators in meeting the updated criteria, Google has started rolling out diagnostic toolsets within the Play Console.These integrated monitoring dashboards allow development teams to evaluate and fine-tune their titles to stay within acceptable performance bounds across different RAM tiers, application categories and process states.
Article Summary: Google Play is introducing strict performance benchmarks to lower app memory footprints. New standards for secure device migration during user upgrades. Google Play will require published Android App Bundles to achieve at least 25% coverage using code-shrinking, optimisation and obfuscation utilities like R8.
